analysis: Both units contain only BASE excerpts of docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (lines 1–422). No HEAD text, patch or implementation source is supplied, so changed security behavior and PR-introduced regressions cannot be established. Relevant baseline contracts for T-041, TB-007 and A-001 include pinned-volume/no-follow I/O (27–32, 66–75), authenticated encrypted payloads and keyed filenames (41–64), encrypted checkpoint token/scope manifests (105–119), strict import identity checks (147–153), bounded fallback with retirement/refund sequencing (173–196), and epoch binding (198–212). Availability/wear controls include demand admission and write budgets (273–281, 288–304), staging limits (282–286), and fail-closed accounting (295–298). Integration must compare the actual changes and trace SSDNoFollowIO, SSDCacheEpochStore, SSDHybridCheckpointStore read/write/maintenance, native import retirement, and factory/policy callers. Confirm authenticated account salt isolation, 30-minute maximum TTL, KEK purge and metadata confidentiality remain intact; validate durable-ready publication after write/engine retirement (123), eviction before publication (392–399), and telemetry exposure (407–411). The baseline document describes optional resident retention (336), whereas canonical T-041 states production constructs no resident cache; this alone does not establish a new PR issue. Actual factory changes are needed to assess whether the threat model requires updating. Authorization, billing and encryption cross-file effects remain unverified without the changed source.
